item.title: Refactor orders order status from String to OrderStatus enum
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, local socket): The `orders` crate stores an order's status as a `String` and compares string literals all over the code. Refactor it to a proper type.

- Add `src/status.rs` with `pub enum OrderStatus { Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled }` deriving at least `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash`.
- `OrderStatus::as_str(self) -> &'static str` returns the lowercase names ("pending", "paid", "shipped", "cancelled"); `Display` prints the same.
- `FromStr` for `OrderStatus` with `type Err = ParseStatusError`, a public error type that implements `std::error::Error` and whose message names the rejected input.
- `OrderStatus::can_transition_to(self, next: OrderStatus) -> bool` encodes the lifecycle: pending -> paid, pending -> cancelled, paid -> shipped, paid -> cancelled; nothing else.
- `Order::status` becomes an `OrderStatus`; re-export `OrderStatus` and `ParseStatusError` from the crate root; use the enum everywhere, so the status string literals appear only in `src/status.rs`.

Observable behaviour (errors, report output and ordering, parsing) must stay exactly the same, and `cargo test` must pass. Commit the work on the local branch (ship mode is local; do not push). Use the commit identity already configured in the repository; do not add attribution lines.

stages.summary:
BASELINE + CHARACTERIZATION (attempt 1; no feedback to address).

Structural goal (for refactorer): replace Order::status (String) with a pub enum OrderStatus {Pending, Paid, Shipped, Cancelled} in src/status.rs (as_str, Display, FromStr with ParseStatusError, can_transition_to: pending->paid|cancelled, paid->shipped|cancelled), re-export OrderStatus and ParseStatusError from the crate root, and keep status literals only in status.rs. Observable behaviour must not change.

Commits:
- Original baseline: ea47a3b01a9b9d34f7575a6e62573e99d22afb01 (tree 6e35d20143ea2a04a1a2774dbb91a210c78ccdcf) — "bench fixture".
- 821c633 test: characterize order status transitions and refusal messages (tests/characterization_transitions.rs, 6 tests)
- 0dfe960 test: characterize status reports and line parsing (tests/characterization_reports.rs, 13 tests)
- Current HEAD 0dfe960098d4d216c4cf75ef4daf84da0bfc2c05, tree 9571bf9b4ff71e6361dbe44822ca9cb93eb799d1. No production code or existing tests were changed.

Checks (no README, CI, Makefile or Justfile exists; the Cargo manifest is the only source of commands). Toolchain cargo 1.98.1.
- Before any test changes, at baseline ea47a3b: `cargo test` exit 0 (3 tests pass); `cargo build` exit 0; `cargo clippy --all-targets` exit 0, no warnings; `cargo fmt --check` exit 1. The fmt failure is pre-existing: src/billing.rs:2, src/order.rs:23, src/report.rs:15 and :23, src/shipping.rs:2, tests/orders.rs:40 are not rustfmt-clean. I did not reformat them, since that is outside this stage.
- After adding tests, at HEAD 0dfe960: `cargo test` exit 0 (22 tests: 3 original, 6 transition, 13 report/parse, all pass); `cargo clippy --all-targets` exit 0, no warnings; the new test files are rustfmt-clean. `cargo fmt --check` still exits 1 only on the pre-existing files above.
- Build outputs are in the item cache (CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.../.archon/data/cache/refactor-order-status/items/qi_01M8AHCY8X2QFHDG6A52ZXSS3Q/cargo-target). Logs there: clippy-baseline.log, test-after.log, fmt-after.log, test-final.log.
- No servers or processes were started.

Public surface to preserve (inventory):
- orders::Order { pub id: u32, pub customer: String, pub total_cents: u64, pub status: String } derives Debug, Clone, PartialEq. Allowed exception from the brief: the type of `status` changes to OrderStatus. Order::new(u32, &str, u64) -> Order starts pending. Order::is_open(&self) -> bool is true for pending|paid. Order::cancel(&mut self) -> Result<(), String>: refused for shipped|cancelled.
- billing::pay(&mut Order) -> Result<(), String> (pending only); billing::outstanding_cents(&[Order]) -> u64 (sums pending only).
- shipping::ship(&mut Order) -> Result<(), String> (paid only); shipping::ready_to_ship(&[Order]) -> Vec<u32> (input order).
- report::status_counts(&[Order]) -> Vec<(String, usize)>. Keep the String type; the brief does not allow changing it. Output is sorted by status NAME (cancelled, paid, pending, shipped), NOT lifecycle order.
- report::to_line(&Order) -> String = "id,customer,total_cents,status" with no escaping.
- report::from_line(&str) -> Result<Order, String>. It trims only the outer whitespace of the line. Field count is checked first ("expected 4 fields, got N"), then id, then total, then status. Status check is exact and case-sensitive ("unknown status \"X\""). Parse errors are `bad id "x": <ParseIntError>` and `bad total ...`.
- Exact error strings: "order N cannot be paid: it is S", "order N cannot be shipped: it is S", "order N cannot be cancelled: it is S", where S is the lowercase status name.
- Status names as text: pending, paid, shipped, cancelled.
- Not public: KNOWN const in report.rs.

Coverage now pinned: all lifecycle transitions and refusals (pay, ship, cancel, is_open), error texts for every refused state, status_counts ordering including shipped, outstanding_cents and ready_to_ship filtering and order, to_line/from_line round trip for all statuses, from_line errors (field count, bad id/total incl. overflow and negative, empty id, unknown or case-mismatched status, check order), whitespace trimming behaviour, and the comma-in-customer case.
The new tests use only `order.status.to_string()` (Display) and never the field's type, so they should stay valid after the change. Test helpers that match on status strings are in the test files, which is fine per the brief.

Known gaps: no CLI or file IO exists to test; to_line/from_line edge cases beyond those listed are not pinned; there is no test that calls can_transition_to (that is new API). The refactorer should not change error text or from_line's check order.

Feedback: none on attempt 1. Carried forward for the refactorer: the pre-existing fmt failures are not part of this change. Run `cargo fmt` only if the refactor touches those lines, and say so.

pr.body:
Approach: add src/status.rs with OrderStatus (as_str, Display via f.pad, FromStr, can_transition_to) and ParseStatusError (Display matches the old 'unknown status {:?}' text). Re-export both from the crate root. Order::status becomes OrderStatus. pay, ship and cancel check can_transition_to, which encodes exactly the previous guards (pending->paid, paid->shipped, pending|paid->cancelled). outstanding_cents and ready_to_ship filter on enum equality. status_counts still returns String names, using BTreeMap<&'static str> so ordering is byte-identical to the old sort. from_line parses via FromStr, keeping the field-count, id, total, status check order.

Key files: src/status.rs (new), src/lib.rs, src/order.rs, src/billing.rs, src/shipping.rs, src/report.rs.

Checks: cargo test exit 0, 26 tests (4 new unit tests in status.rs; 13 report/parse and 6 transition characterization tests; 3 original). cargo build exit 0. cargo clippy --all-targets exit 0, no warnings. Characterization and original tests unmodified. cargo fmt --check: only pre-existing tests/orders.rs:40 remains; the touched lines in billing, order, report and shipping were rustfmt-formatted as part of the rewrite.

Assumptions and limits: the only public API change is the brief-authorized Order::status type. External callers that compare status to a string must now use the enum or to_string(). No CLI or file IO exists to test beyond the characterization suite.
pr.summary: made order status a typed enum. now can match and transition statuses without string literals; invalid names fail at parse time. before: Order::status was a String compared against literals in billing, shipping, order and report; now: Order::status is OrderStatus with can_transition_to, and string literals live only in src/status.rs. Behaviour, error text and report output unchanged.
pr.title: refactor: use OrderStatus enum for order status

risk.why: Breaking public API change: Order is a pub struct and its pub status field changes from String to OrderStatus, which breaks any downstream reader or writer of that field. The change is brief-authorized and touches 4 small src files, with no behaviour change, verified by 19 characterization and original tests passing unchanged plus 4 new unit tests. Per the rubric, API changes that break callers and large cross-cutting refactors are high, so it is rated high when in doubt.
